title: Add e2e integration tests with Splunk HEC + Datadog Logs sandboxes
author: Leila Farouk
release_notes: Internal only: adds docker-compose-based e2e harness and CI job for validating Splunk HEC + Datadog Logs adapters end-to-end (including throttling + dedup expectations).
description: Context: As part of SIEM-ready audit export beta, we need repeatable end-to-end confidence that the exporter can deliver to downstreams with realistic failure modes (auth errors, 429 throttling, payload validation issues) and that our retry/backoff + checkpointing semantics behave as expected. This PR adds an integration test suite + docker-compose-ish harness that boots the exporter alongside (a) a Splunk-like HEC stub service and (b) a Datadog Logs intake stub service. It does not attempt to fully emulate Splunk/Datadog; it’s focused on request/response behavior the adapters depend on. Scope: - New `e2e/` harness with compose config for local + CI runs - Splunk HEC stub: validates token header, supports `/services/collector/event` + `/services/collector/health`, can simulate 429s and partial failures - Datadog stub: validates API key header, supports `/api/v2/logs`, can simulate 403 (bad key), 429 (rate limit), and payload schema errors - E2E tests that drive synthetic audit events through the exporter pipeline and assert: (1) delivery occurs, (2) retry/backoff on 429, (3) idempotency/dedup expectations at the destination boundary, (4) metrics emitted (lag, retries, adapter errors) - CI wiring: add a gated job that runs on PRs touching adapters/export pipeline; run time ~6–8 min on standard runners Notes/limitations: - The stubs persist received events to a local volume and expose a `/received` endpoint for assertions. - Tests are intentionally strict about headers/content-type/encoding because we’ve seen regressions around compression and batching. - This suite assumes the existing local dev harness can inject synthetic audit events into the exporter (see `scripts/dev/seed_audit_events.ts`); the test wrapper calls it directly. - No real Splunk/Datadog containers are used in CI; those are flaky and require extra licensing/credentials. Related: ENG-5195. Follow-ups: (1) add S3 path to harness (separate PR), (2) add chaos mode for long downstream outage + auto-pause behavior (tracked in ENG-1119 follow-up work).
commits: test(e2e): add docker-compose harness for exporter + SIEM stubs
test(stubs): implement splunk-hec stub with throttling + auth validation
test(stubs): implement datadog logs intake stub with 403/429 modes
test(e2e): add delivery + retry + dedup assertions for splunk and datadog adapters
ci: add e2e job and tighten timeouts for deterministic runs
docs: add local instructions for running e2e suite and debugging failures
conversation: Leila Farouk (author): Added e2e harness + stubs for Splunk HEC and Datadog Logs. Main goal is catching adapter regressions and validating retry/backoff under throttling. I kept it license-free by using lightweight Node stubs instead of real Splunk/Datadog. Would love eyes from SRE/Telemetry on whether assertions + timeouts are reasonable for CI.

Sean Gallagher (reviewer): Love the direction. Two asks: (1) please ensure tests fail fast and don’t hang if exporter never becomes healthy; (2) we should assert on exporter metrics to catch cases where we silently drop to DLQ. Can we add a minimum set of metrics checks?

Leila Farouk (author): Yep. I’ll add an explicit readiness gate with a 60s timeout (`/healthz` + `/readyz`) and wire a metrics scrape from the exporter to assert `audit_export_delivery_success_total` increments and `audit_export_adapter_dlq_total` stays at 0 for the happy path.

Logan Wright (reviewer): Metrics naming: we’ve standardized on `redwood_audit_exporter_*`. I see you’re asserting `audit_export_delivery_success_total` in one test; can we update to the prefixed name and avoid label cardinality traps? Also please don’t assert on exact histogram buckets (they change).

Leila Farouk (author): Good catch. Updated assertions to (a) use `redwood_audit_exporter_delivery_success_total`, (b) assert on counter deltas only, and (c) avoid histogram bucket checks. Also removed `tenant_id` label from stub-emitted logs; tests now rely on `workspace_id_hash` like prod.

Colin O'Donnell (reviewer): For the Splunk stub: can we simulate Splunk’s common partial-success response where `code=0` but some events include `text="Invalid data format"`? We’ve had customers hit this. Even a simplified version would help.

Leila Farouk (author): Added `SPLUNK_STUB_MODE=partial_fail` which returns a mixed response and verifies exporter marks the batch as failed (so it retries with backoff) rather than checkpointing past it. Included a regression test named `splunk_hec_partial_failure_retries.test.ts`.

Caleb Johnson (reviewer): CI concern: compose on GitHub runners can be flaky if we rely on port reuse. Please pin explicit ports and add `--project-name` randomization to avoid collisions. Also, can you cap logs so failures don’t exceed artifacts limits?

Leila Farouk (author): Updated `run_e2e.sh` to create a unique compose project name using `${GITHUB_RUN_ID:-local}` and pinned ports to an ephemeral range computed from a hash (falls back to defaults for local). Added log truncation in the workflow and upload of last 5k lines for each container on failure.
Sean Gallagher (reviewer): One more nit: the 429 retry test uses real sleeps of 30s+ (backoff). That’ll make CI slow. Can we inject a backoff multiplier for tests?

Leila Farouk (author): Added `EXPORTER_BACKOFF_SCALE` env var (defaults to 1.0, set to 0.05 in e2e) so the retry behavior is exercised without long wall clock time. Also added a guard to ensure we still observe multiple retries (>=2) so the test doesn’t become meaningless.
CI Bot: e2e-siem-harness failed: `retry_backoff_429.test.ts` timed out waiting for received count. Artifacts uploaded: exporter.log, splunk.log, datadog.log.

Leila Farouk (author): Root cause: exporter was starting before configs were applied; tests began seeding events too early. Fixed by waiting for `GET /v1/status` to report at least one active destination before seeding. Re-ran CI.
Logan Wright (reviewer): Looks good now. Approving. Please file a follow-up to add S3 to the harness; it’s the other major beta destination.
Leila Farouk (author): Will do (new Linear task incoming).
Sean Gallagher (reviewer): Approved. From SRE side: thanks for adding readiness timeouts + artifact capture. This will help on-call a ton when we get flakes.
Maintainer (squash merge): Merged via squash. Thanks!
